top_story: By 28 September, renewed fighting in Yemen was already pushing children out of school and into labor, showing how even localized escalation quickly hardens into long-term social damage for poor households. A day earlier in Gaza, aid workers were confronting 61 million tonnes of rubble that may still conceal up to 10,000 bodies, underscoring that the war’s aftermath is not a post-conflict phase but an ongoing humanitarian and psychological emergency. Against that backdrop, Bezalel Smotrich’s 27 September call for a Gaza-style full-scale war in the occupied West Bank, including dismantling the Palestinian Authority, signaled pressure to widen Israel’s campaign model from enclave destruction to deeper territorial and political reengineering. The regional picture is one of conflict regimes that do not only kill and displace, but also erase civic institutions, education, and the material basis of recovery.
